page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.r7a.16xlarge demonstrates strong performance in several key areas. Its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top 25%, supported by strong PassMark CPU, extended instructions, and encryption scores. Memory performance is also notable, with small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores placing in the top 25%. However, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths fall into the average tier. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench ray tracing, and image processing also show strong results, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput remain in the average range.

The instance offers high resource density and dedicated CPU allocation, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that require consistent compute performance without virtualization overhead. The lack of local storage requires external block storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. Given its high memory capacity and strong multi-threaded processing capabilities, this server is well-suited for large-scale in-memory databases, memory-intensive data processing, enterprise applications, and moderate-scale language model inference.

Conversely, large-block uncached memory bandwidth, database operations, and static web serving throughput perform in the average tier. With a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps, the instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads. It is highly suited for in-memory databases, large-scale data processing, and enterprise applications that require substantial memory capacity without the need for local NVMe storage.
